newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhs say oil exchanges with Iran to start soon.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhs say oil exchanges with Iran to start soon.

text.p: Oil-rich but landlocked Kazakhstan will soon start oil exchanges with Iran, the Central Asian nation's deputy foreign minister said on Thursday.
"The last technical problems in connection with oil volumes have been decided," Kazakh Deputy Foreign Minister Vladimir Alesin told a news conference in the Kazakh capital Almaty.
Alesin said the two countries' differences over long-planned exchanges had centred on oil quality.
He gave no details of volumes or when the exchanges will begin, but Iranian officials said in August the oil swaps would total around two million tonnes annually.

Under the scheme, which will help more Kazakh oil to reach world markets, Kazakhstan will ship oil across the Caspian Sea south to Iran's Caspian coast. Iran will make available for Kazakhstan the equivalent amount in the Gulf.
"The oil route to the south...is for Kazakhstan the shortest and most economical," Alesin said.
Last week, Iranian officials proposed an oil export pipeline linking the two countries.

However, the United States, with many oil majors investing in the region, opposes any strengthening of ties between the former Soviet republics of Central Asia and neighbouring Iran because of what Washington says is Tehran's involvement in terrorism.
Almost all of Kazakhstan's oil is now exported through the Russian system, but Moscow has been unwilling to give Almaty --Chris Bird, Almaty Newsroom +7 3272 509410
